items.title: Joe Lyde Interview, 1959-05-18
items.q: I heard them and I heard Littleton Littleton's band and that was much better to my mind

ctx.x: And he played, tried to play, he used to play all, I remember I had an old record of Bunk playing Tishomingo blues on Brunswick and hear the Crane River band and they'd play every note identically, you know, an old clarinet phrase coming through. No drums, Collier was always very particular about drums, he said until he could find a drummer that was fit to play with a New Orleans band, he wasn't gonna have one. He just had a two string, three string bass, trombone, Julian Davis, he wore a fez, and Pat Hawes on…

and Moose March which is always copied straight from Russell's I think Russell's got one Moose March hasn't he or somebody's got one of punk he may have yeah I think so I think I've heard it somewhere I don't know whether it was Russell or one of those other early fellows that recorded down here and I heard them and I heard Littleton Littleton's band and that was much better to my mind it was much more lively much less much more imagination much looser they weren't in they weren't they didn't really worry if they…

I heard something maybe Mike's ladder mm-hmm told me that they consider over in England now that if a person starts playing traditional that if he gets any better they have to start playing a different style of music until he gets so good that he's playing progressive do you know anything about
